h: Shabbos Calms Sorrow Over the Past and Future Fear

p: according to what is stated in the holy Zohar
"On the day that Hashem gives you rest
from your sorrow and from your fear, etc.,"
that damage occurred in one's deeds,
and it is not possible to repair it.
is the dread about the future,
lest it trip him up again,
like the matter of "A person should always incite
the good inclination against the evil inclination" (Berachos 5a),
that is, so that it not trip him up.
the holiness of the day of Shabbos
for his heart is firm and secure
that he will be guarded from now on
And with this one can understand
is the outcry in the heart
and the sorrow over the past;
over the dread of the future.
And it is stated about this
that the matter of the outcry over the past
is alluded to in the pasuk (Bereishis 27:22):
"The voice is the voice of Yaakov";
that the voice of Yaakov's outcry
is from what was done to him by
as is stated in the Gemara
is the matter of anger and jealousy,
and it is the utmost distance
as is known from the metzora,
even from the camp of Yisrael,
from the blemish of anger and jealousy;
and this has no place at all
when a person senses in his soul
that he has some touch of this,
the outcry in his heart grows,
כְּעִנְיַן צָעֲקוּ וַה׳ שָׁמֵעַ (תְּהִלִּים לד, יח)
like "They cried out, and Hashem heard" (Tehillim 34:18);
and as is stated in the Midrash
are called by the name Mitzrayim,
is the root of the kelipah of desire;
which is why it is called
וַאֲשֶׁר בְּשַׂר חֲמוֹרִים בְּשָׂרָם (יְחֶזְקֵאל כג, כ)
and "whose flesh is the flesh of donkeys" (Yechezkel 23:20),
and this is the kelipah of Yishmael.
And it is the oppressor and embitterer
that it is not in his power
the most pious of the pious, etc."
וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תַּזְרִיעַ, יד, ה)
therefore it is not sent away
for it is destined to be whitened
that is, the yetzer hara of desire
And regarding the two matters mentioned above,
when the day of Shabbos arrives
that there is born moreover because of them
that is, that purity comes to the body
of the radiance of a person's face;
מַה שֶּׁעַל הַהֵיפֶךְ נֶאֱמַר (אִיּוֹב יד, כ)
whereas of the opposite it is said (Iyov 14:20):
"You change his face and send him away."
and there is not mentioned here
which correspond to ruach and nefesh.
For the dwelling of the nefesh
and it is the level of Esav,
as is stated in the holy Zohar
And the dwelling of the ruach is in the heart;
and the leaven in the dough
הוּא מִלֵּב כְּסִיל לִשְׂמֹאלוֹ (קֹהֶלֶת י, ב)
is from "the heart of a fool is to his left" (Koheles 10:2),
and it is the kelipah of desire
"It is revealed and known before You
that our will is to do Your will,
but the leaven in the dough holds us back";
of which a small amount is good,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א כט, יח)
as the inclination of the thoughts of the heart of Your people, etc."
